title: Greensboro Mayor-Elect Marikay Abuzuaiter clarifies email regarding representation: 'Rules and protocol we have to follow - NewsBreak
text:
By Cassie Fambro ,
1 hours ago
GREENSBORO, N.C. (WGHP) — As incoming Greensboro Mayor Marikay Abuzuaiter gets ready to transition into her role, she’s working to set ground rules and help make sure the six new city council members are prepared for their jobs.
An email recently sent to the council raised some eyebrows, with Abuzuaiter stating she is “the face and the only spokesperson for the city and council on council matters.”
Upon receipt of the letter, three of the new council members, Crystal Black, Cecile Crawford and Adam Marshall, replied with questions regarding the official policies and what responsibility they have to the mayor.
A public records request yielded a copy of the Nov. 12 letter in which Abuzuaiter says she wants council members to be “mindful” about a few things.
“I sent it out just as a welcome, and I wanted them to know there are things the mayor does,” Abuzuaiter said.
She says that does not mean council members will be boxed in or can’t speak on behalf of their districts.
“This does not mean that any council member can’t go to a neighborhood meeting, go to anything else. It is good to let the chair of the board know … if you are having a meeting that involves city staff, city employees,” Abuzuaiter said.
If a meeting involves city staff or employees, City Manager Trey Davis has to know about it. “
“He and the city attorney are two employees. They are the only two employees we can direct at all,” she said, citing state law.
As for council members themselves, she says they need to keep each other in the loop with regard to sunshine laws.
“If five of us meet, that has to be noticed as a council meeting,” she said.
In regards to the email, she says her intention was not to discourage anyone.
“I am not there to tell anybody ‘no.’ I want to say ‘yes,’ and we go from there to see how it can be done or if it can be done because there are a lot of rules and protocol we have to follow first,” she said.
Abuzuaiter says she’s also hyper-aware that her emails are under scrutiny
“I know every time I do an email, it’s public record. I have no issue with that. I am fine with that, and anyone who wants to look at it can look at it,” she said.
With six new council members, there’s a lot to learn, and she wants to help.
“They have my numbers and have my emails, and they can text me anytime, day or night,” Abuzuaiter said.
The new council had a formal orientation on Monday and were able to discuss the email and any other questions in person.
FOX8 also reached out to Marshall, Black and Crawford. Two responded, indicating their questions were answered by the mayor. The first meeting with the new council is on Dec. 16.
